rounds.text: Unihealth Hospitals Ltd demonstrates exceptional top and bottom-line expansion, led by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 38% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 39% [E14, E17]. This momentum has accelerated recently, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 33% and profit growth of 81% [E16, E19], alongside a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 yielding a buy recommendation [E59]. The business operates with elite capital efficiency, generating a return on equity of 38.04% and a return on capital employed of 33.03%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 10.45% and 12.06% [E9, E10]. Valuation multiples offer a compelling entry point relative to growth and peers, with a P/E of 22.03x against a sector benchmark of 30.81x and an EV/EBITDA of 10.05x against a sector benchmark of 16.62x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models indicate a substantial margin of safety of 59.7%, with today's market price implying an earnings growth rate of just 5.5% compared to an 18.0% base-case assumption [E41, E42]. The balance sheet remains conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.24x and a comfortable current ratio of 5.33x [E32, E33]. Conceded: [E29], [E31], [E36], [E37], [E38], [E58].

Unihealth Hospitals Ltd carries substantial underlying risks that undermine its headline growth figures, notably highlighted by an alarming cash conversion ratio of 0.13x for March 2026 where profits far outpace actual cash generation, paired with exceptionally high debtors of 341 days [E29, E58]. This severe disconnect between reported earnings and cash realization results in a negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr, while borrowings have simultaneously increased from Rs 22 Cr to Rs 33 Cr [E31, E34]. Institutional confidence is visibly eroding, evidenced by foreign institutions slashing their stake from 5.61% to 0.01% and domestic institutions reducing holdings from 3.31% to 0.45% since September 2023, accompanied by negative institutional money flow and recent promoter selling [E37, E38, E39, E56]. Furthermore, technical and operational momentum is faltering, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, quarterly operating margin contracting by 5 percentage points year-over-year, and earnings growth explicitly flagged as decelerating [E26, E45, E64]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical sales and profit compounding alongside impressive return metrics such as an ROE of 38.04% versus a sector benchmark of 10.45% [E9, E14, E17].

Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.13x for March 2026 and debtors are high at 341 days [E29, E58], yet this has not prevented stellar top-line and bottom-line compounding, with 5-year sales growth at 38% and profit growth at 39% [E14, E17]. Conceded: free cash flow is negative at Rs -26 Cr and borrowings rose to Rs 33 Cr [E31, E34], but the company maintains a very comfortable current ratio of 5.33x alongside a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.24x [E32, E33]. Conceded: institutional holdings and quarterly margins have declined alongside moving average trends [E26, E37, E38, E45], but these backward-looking or sentiment-driven indicators are overshadowed by an elite return profile featuring an ROE of 38.04% and ROCE of 33.03% that vastly outperform sector benchmarks of 10.45% and 12.06% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is actively scaling for future expansion, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress doubling with a 100% surge to Rs 10 Cr [E35]. Most importantly, the market price at ₹ 475 is heavily discounted against a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 1179, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 59.7% [E2, E40, E41].

Conceded: the 5-year sales and profit growth figures sit at 38% and 39% respectively [E14, E17], but backward-looking compounding offers little comfort when recent reality shows sharp deceleration and heavy price-to-earnings expansion to 29.5x [E1, E64]. The bull points to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.24x and strong liquidity [E32, E33], but ignores that borrowings climbed to Rs 33 Cr while free cash flow plunged to a negative Rs -26 Cr [E31, E34]. The claim that elite ROE and ROCE metrics overshadow declining institutional support and weakening quarterly margins [E9, E10, E26, E37, E38] completely dismisses fundamental operational red flags: cash conversion sits at an abysmal 0.13x because profits vastly outpace actual cash, and debtors stand at an alarming 341 days [E29, E58]. Conceded: Capital Work in Progress doubled to Rs 10 Cr to fund expansion [E35], yet this capex build-up phase has triggered negative free cash flow alongside a 100% surge in CWIP without guaranteed commercial completion. Finally, relying on a DCF model for a margin of safety [E40, E41] ignores that the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages amid negative institutional money flow, 69.5% annualized volatility, and a price-led expectation mismatch where price growth recently outran profit growth by 110% [E39, E45, E49, E52].

Conceded: quarterly operating margins softened by 5 percentage points [E26], and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 26 Cr [E31]. However, the bear's alarm over cash conversion and receivables overlooks the actual operating cash flow of Rs 6 Cr and a robust current ratio of 5.33x [E30, E33]. While borrowings rose to Rs 33 Cr, the debt-to-equity ratio remains conservatively low at 0.24x [E32, E34], fully supporting the doubled CWIP of Rs 10 Cr earmarked for future growth [E35]. The criticism of moving averages and institutional holdings [E37, E38, E45] dismisses the fundamental reality of a sector-beating 38.04% ROE against a 10.45% benchmark and a 33.03% ROCE against 12.06% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the valuation is hardly stretched when viewed through the lens of a 10.05x EV/EBITDA ratio that sits well below the sector benchmark of 16.62x [E11]. Finally, the rules-based screen validates this strength with a solid 86 out of 100 score, driven by powerful sales and profit growth metrics [E59, E60, E62].

Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.24x and the current ratio is 5.33x [E32, E33]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash concerns ignores the stark reality that cash conversion has collapsed to 0.13x alongside extreme debtor days reaching 341 [E29, E58]. While the bull points to operating cash flow of Rs 6 Cr and low EV/EBITDA, it glosses over a severe negative free cash flow of Rs 26 Cr and rising borrowings of Rs 33 Cr [E11, E30, E31, E34]. The high ROE and ROCE figures are severely undermined by a dangerously low tax rate flag and reported earnings growth deceleration [E9, E10, E57, E64]. Furthermore, the technical and institutional picture reveals a stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages accompanied by a negative money flow and severe institutional exit [E37, E38, E39, E45]. Finally, price growth has raced ahead of profit growth by 110%, making the high screening score vulnerable to evaporating expectations [E52, E59].
